name: Mangaladevi Temple
architecturalStyle: Indigenous Kerala-Tulunadu timber and laterite sloping tiled roof
anchorSignificance: Eponymous deity of Mangalore, established by Matsyendranath and King Kundavarma.

name: Kadri Manjunatha Temple
architecturalStyle: Laterite tiered sanctum housing 10th-century world-famous bronze icons
anchorSignificance: Living harmony of Natha yogic hermitage, Vajrayana Buddhism, and Shaivism.

name: Kateel Sri Durgaparameshwari Temple
architecturalStyle: River-island sanctum constructed within the flowing bed of Nandini river
anchorSignificance: World center for Harake Yakshagana and Agni Keli fire rituals.

name: Polali Sri Rajarajeshwari Temple
architecturalStyle: Famed for 10-foot clay medicinal idol (Lepa Murti) and copper-sheeted gopuram
anchorSignificance: Site of Polali Chendu sports ritual and ancient terracotta sculpture.

name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
deity: Lord Krishna (Navaneetha Krishna with churning rod)
architecturalStyle: Ashta Matha monastic quadrangle around Madhwa Sarovara and Kanakana Kindi
anchorSignificance: Global fountainhead of Dvaita Vedanta philosophy and Paryaya monastic rotational governance.

name: Kukke Sri Subramanya Temple
deity: Lord Subramanya (Guha / Kartikeya) protecting Serpent King Vasuki
era: Ancient / Puranic mentions in Skanda Purana
architecturalStyle: Laterite courtyards at the foot of Western Ghats peak Kumara Parvatha
anchorSignificance: Supreme pan-Indian sanctuary for Sarpa Samskara and Ashlesha Bali rites.

name: Gokarna Mahabaleshwara Temple
architecturalStyle: Granite and laterite Dravidian-Konkan hybrid with sunken Saligrama peetha
anchorSignificance: Dakshina Kashi housing the Atmalinga retrieved from Ravana by Ganesha.

name: Bappanadu Durgaparameshwari Temple
architecturalStyle: Expansive courtyard with massive Dhwajasthambha and Dolu drum pavilion
anchorSignificance: Symbol of Hindu-Muslim coastal syncretism built through the partnership of Goddess Durga and merchant Bappa Byari.

name: Sri Kshetra Dharmasthala
deity: Lord Manjunatha (Shiva) and Four Dharma Daivas
architecturalStyle: Sprawling temple city flanked by the Netravati river
anchorSignificance: Unique tri-religious synthesis: Jain Heggade custodianship, Vaishnava Madhwa priesthood, Shaivite deity, and folk Daivas.

name: Kollur Sri Mookambika Temple
era: Ancient / Consecrated by Adi Shankaracharya (8th Century CE)
architecturalStyle: Kerala-Coastal wood-copper architecture with golden crest and Shankara Peetha
anchorSignificance: Premier Shakta Vidya Peetha of South India where thousands initiate children into writing (Vidyarambha).
